analysis:
Scope: Sandbox CLI work-disk support (TB-013, A-019, T-061; storage-trust parallels T-041 external APFS notes). No regressions found.

SandboxWorkDisk.swift (new, head 1-194):
- statfs-based volume probe (50-69).
- APFS and ownership checks (72-110).
- Candidate listing of /Volumes (173-184): requires local, writable, non-hidden, APFS, an exact mount-point match and minimum free space.
- enableOwnership (120-121): a new privileged path. It runs /usr/bin/sudo with an argv array and `--`, fixed absolute /usr/sbin/diskutil, and the statfs-derived absolute mount point. There is no shell, so no injection, and a leading '-' is not possible.
- runInForeground (129-157) uses posix_spawn with CLOEXEC_DEFAULT and inherits only fds 0-2. It requires a foreground tty, and sudo prompts for the password itself.
- environ is passed through; sudo env_reset applies. This was not verified here.
- shellWord (187-193) is display-only quoting and correctly escapes single quotes.

Setup and installer rechecks:
- Setup checks are advisory pre-checks. The comment at lines 5-7 says the installer rechecks each disk under the add-on's full rules before writing; the installer source is outside this evidence.
- There is a TOCTOU window between the CLI check and installer use. It is not material because the installer already runs as the owner (TB-013).

SandboxSetupProgress.swift (head 162-204):
- New parsing of plan `disks` from installer stdout.
- Uses type-checked casts and drops malformed entries; data is display/sizing only.

SandboxStatusView.diskLines (head 189-203):
- Renders add-on-reported path, state and detail strings to the terminal.
- The same class of add-on-supplied text (detail, installer text lines) was already printed before this PR, and the add-on is owner-installed code. Terminal-escape exposure is therefore not new.

Tests (SandboxStatusTests 76-99) are fixtures only.

Threat-model note for integration:
- TB-013/T-061 could mention that the CLI can now invoke `sudo diskutil enableOwnership` on an owner-selected volume. It is interactive and owner-confirmed, so it is not a finding.
- Callers of enableOwnership/candidates (the setup command, --disk plumbing to install.sh) were not in this batch. Integration should confirm the CLI prompts before running sudo and passes only absolutePath()-normalized paths to the installer.
